title: Regular Expression Denial of Service in html-minifier (reCustomIgnore)
affectedRange: <= 4.0.0 (all published versions; the html-minifier-terser successor is also affected)
shortFix: Patches CVE-2022-37620 (ReDoS) by bounding the leading whitespace in the custom-fragment regex, making matching linear.
longFix: The `reCustomIgnore` regex `\s*(?:<%...%>|<?...?>)+\s*` had an unbounded leading `\s*` that backtracks catastrophically on long whitespace runs not followed by a fragment. Bounding only the leading whitespace to 100 characters makes matching linear; output is identical for all realistic input (verified by a 75-case cross-version equivalence test).
summary: html-minifier's `minify()` replaces "ignored custom fragments" (template tags like `<%...%>` and `<?...?>`) via the `reCustomIgnore` regular expression `\s*(?:...)+\s*`. The leading `\s*` backtracks catastrophically: input containing a long run of whitespace not followed by a fragment makes `minify()` take time quadratic in the input length (a ~160 KB string takes ~40 seconds), so untrusted HTML can hang the event loop. Note: the widely-used successor `html-minifier-terser` ships the identical regex and is also affected; at the time of writing there is no fixed version of either on npm.
poc:
const { minify } = require('html-minifier');
minify('x' + ' '.repeat(200000) + '!'); // hangs for many seconds on 4.0.0
fixExplanation: The leading `\s*` in `reCustomIgnore` is bounded to `\s{0,100}`. The trailing `\s*` is left unbounded because it only runs after a fragment has matched and therefore never backtracks. No real template has 100+ whitespace characters immediately before an ignored fragment, so minified output is byte-for-byte identical for realistic input — confirmed across 75 input/option combinations against the original. Matching is now linear (a 2 MB worst-case input completes in well under a second).
